description: Simulator measurements (irl-subt-9ij.20): Moonshine Base load 34.6 s, CAM++ 3.8 s, streaming Silero VAD RTF 2.1 (67 ms per 32 ms window). jsc shell with the same asyncify build: Silero 0.58 ms/window, so the web process adds ~100x somewhere. Hypotheses: timer/rAF throttling of an occluded or background WebView, worker scheduling, Cache Storage body reads, transformers.js overhead, message passing per window. Profile in the simulator (Web Inspector / console timings from A0), fix or document, and check whether iOS WKWebView behaves the same.

comments.text: Explained, no code change needed beyond kdl.2. Evidence: (1) jsc shell (same JSC as the simulator), asyncify build: Silero 0.58 ms/window, Moonshine q4 decoder create 5.1 s, first encoder run 8.0 s; plain build 0.40 ms, 0.6 s, 0.17 s. (2) Simulator after kdl.2 (plain build in CPU workers): VAD RTF 0.015-0.018 (= jsc shell), Moonshine Base load 43.2 -> 4.0 s, CAM++ 3.1 -> 0.5 s. So the load time was asyncify. (3) The 'VAD RTF 2.1 / 67 ms per window' figure was measured on 9ij.20's base revision, before the 9ij.16 sample-clock fix; the fixed code measured VAD RTF 0.32 even with asyncify. (4) No timer/rAF throttling in the headless simulator: bench captions record wall time vs captured audio (e.g. t 2.31 s at audio 2.20 s) and the WAV source's 100 ms setInterval stays on time. (5) Remaining gap: transformers.js Moonshine Base decode is ~1.8x slower in the simulator than in Node (950 vs 530 ms per call) - ordinary JSC vs V8 wasm/JS difference; Moonshine Streaming WASM is within 10% of Node. iOS WKWebView uses the same JSC, so the same builds apply; confirm on device in kdl.13.

title: Explain WebKit web-process slowdown beyond asyncify
